title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Reopening a file is cheap again
summary: After reopening a file, the caches paid full price on every request for the rest of the session. A burst of name resolutions cost 29.6 ms instead of 0.28 ms.

highlights.title: The cost of reopening stops there
highlights.description: Comparing the document object is the cheap way to know the text has not changed, and a reopened file gets a new object. The comparison failed forever after, because the entry still pointed at the destroyed one, so every request hashed the whole document.

highlights.title: One helper for the three caches
highlights.description: Folding, semantic tokens and import resolution share the same check now, so they cannot drift apart. The entry adopts the new object once the text is confirmed unchanged, and the next request is free again.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: A file whose content really did change is still detected: the check falls back to comparing the text itself.
Measured over the 40 largest files of a real Android project of 3187 Kotlin files.
